title: Numbers on a Number Line
standard_text: 2.2E locate the position of a given whole number on an open number line; 2.2F name the whole number that corresponds to a specific point on a number line; 2.9C represent whole numbers as distances from any given location on a number line
meta_desc: Free Grade 2 number line worksheets for Texas TEKS 2.2E, 2.2F and 2.9C: name points, count by 2s, 5s, 10s and 100s, locate numbers and find distances. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Find the size of each jump, then count.
key_sub: 300 to 400 in 10 jumps: each jump is 10.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Find the step: how much each jump between tick marks is worth.
  • Start at a number you know and count the jumps.
  • On a number line, numbers get bigger to the right.
  • The distance between two numbers is the bigger number minus the smaller one.

Examples

Example

Line from 300 to 400 with 10 jumps

Each jump is 10

A is 4 jumps after 300

Answer: 340

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Counting the tick marks instead of the jumpsCount the spaces between marks.
Using the wrong stepCheck the labels to find each jump's value.
Starting from 0Start at the first number on the line.
